stories.title: Stotan Acquires Itasca Industrial Facility Near O’Hare International Airport
stories.excerpt: Stotan Industrial, in partnership with 56 Maple, acquired 1101 W. Thorndale Avenue in Itasca, Illinois, a 32,937 square foot industrial facility located in Chicago’s supply constrained O’Hare submarket. Eric Fischer and Gabriel Strauss of Cushman & Wakefield represented the seller in the transaction. Stotan sourced the opportunity through its longstanding relationships in the Chicago industrial market as the owner-user prepared to transition out of the facility. Situated on 2.47 acres in DuPage County, the property offers immediate access to Illinois Route 390, Interstate 290 and Interstate 355. The facility is also approximately 15 minutes from O’Hare International Airport and its South Cargo facilities. “1101 W. Thorndale presented a compelling opportunity to acquire a high-quality industrial asset in one of Chicago’s premier infill markets while providing a long-term facility solution for a growing tenant,” said Blake Waeghe, Development Manager at Stotan. “Buildings of this size and quality are increasingly difficult to acquire in the O’Hare market, particularly in locations offering this level of access and connectivity.” The post Stotan Acquires Itasca Industrial Facility Near O’Hare International Airport appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Stotan Industrial acquires 32,937 SF facility near O'Hare; supply-constrained submarket.
Property on 2.47 acres in DuPage County; 15 minutes from airport cargo.
Owner-user transition signals tight industrial availability in Chicago infill market.
stories.summary: Stotan Industrial and 56 Maple acquired 1101 W. Thorndale Avenue in Itasca, Illinois, a 32,937 square foot industrial facility in Chicago's supply-constrained O'Hare submarket, sourced from an owner-user preparing to vacate. The property sits on 2.47 acres in DuPage County with direct access to I-290, I-355, and Illinois Route 390, approximately 15 minutes from O'Hare's South Cargo facilities. Stotan management noted that buildings of this size and quality are increasingly difficult to acquire in the O'Hare market.
stories.impact: Industrial scarcity near O'Hare—a gateway for goods and logistics—signals strong fundamentals for last-mile logistics but also rising land and development costs in the submarket. This constrains multifamily developers competing for land in nearby submarkets and may drive multifamily site selection further west or south toward lower-cost infill areas in the broader Chicago metro.

stories.title: Sheppard Takes 107K SF at In-Rel’s D.C. Redevelopment
stories.excerpt: One of the 50 highest-grossing law firms in the U.S. has signed an anchor lease at a planned Washington, D.C., trophy office redevelopment three years before its anticipated completion. Law firm Sheppard signed for 107,224 square feet at In-Rel Properties’ 2033 K Street NW, CBRE announced Tuesday. The firm, which has more than 1,200 attorneys across 16 offices, will move in after the building’s expected completion in July 2029. The brokerage did not disclose the value of the lease or the asking rent. In-Rel is expanding and updating the existing building, located along K Street near the intersection of D.C.’s Central Business District, West End and Dupont Circle. The developer will retain the property’s concrete structure while expanding it vertically and horizontally, including adding three floors and a penthouse. The renovations are another example of owners betting on Washington’s bifurcated office market, where distress coexists with a shortage of large, new trophy spaces, particularly for law firms and other high-end tenants. “We all know D.C. has plenty of office space, but what it doesn’t have is enough large-block, trophy-quality product that leading law firms like Sheppard demand,” In-Rel CEO Jackson Siegal said in a statement. Sheppard Chair Luca Salvi said the new office would provide a more modern and efficient workplace as the firm approaches its centennial and continues growing its Washington operation. CBRE’s Dimitri Hajimihalis, Emily Eppolito and Carroll Cavanagh represented In-Rel. Savills’ Gary Stein, David Lipson, Jon Glass and Owen Jaccard represented Sheppard. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Law firm Sheppard signs 107K SF anchor lease at In-Rel's K Street redevelopment.
Building completion July 2029; firm relocating 1,200+ attorneys to D.C.
Trophy office expansion amid bifurcated market: distress and new-supply shortage.
stories.summary: Sheppard, a top-50 U.S. law firm with 1,200+ attorneys across 16 offices, signed a 107,224 square foot anchor lease at In-Rel Properties' 2033 K Street NW in Washington, D.C., three years before the building's anticipated July 2029 completion. In-Rel is expanding and vertically renovating the existing structure, adding three floors and a penthouse while retaining the concrete core. The deal underscores owner confidence in the district's bifurcated office market, where trophy spaces command premiums despite widespread distress.
stories.impact: Large professional-services anchor leases signal sustained demand for premier office in downtown D.C., supporting property valuations and construction lending—but this does NOT drive multifamily demand. Conversely, it may divert capital and construction labor from residential projects and crowd out smaller office conversions to multifamily in the CBD; monitor whether shortage of trophy space accelerates office-to-residential conversions in secondary D.C. office corridors.

stories.title: Eliot Spitzer Gains State Approval to Redevelop 985 Fifth Avenue After Legal Bout
stories.excerpt: Former New York Gov. Eliot Spitzer will finally get to demolish 985 Fifth Avenue after suing the state to obtain approval. Spitzer claimed that the state’s Division of Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) was delaying the approval of an application to not renew rent-stabilized leases in the building, a necessary step before the property could be redeveloped. Spitzer ultimately won the state’s blessing. The two-year request to end the rent-stabilized leases on the property followed approval from the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission in 2023 to take a wrecking ball to the 25-story rental property and construct luxury condominiums in its place. Spitzer alleged potential misconduct in the lawsuit, reported by The Real Deal. Spitzer could not be reached for comment. HCR, now under the administration of Gov. Kathy Hochul, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Spitzer’s Spitzer Enterprises has been advancing on other aspects of the project despite the delay, unveiling designs by SLCE Architects for the property in November 2025 which would yield 25 condo units, according to New York YIMBY. The former governor, who resigned in 2008 during a prostitution scandal, has owned the property since at least 2018 after buying seven residential buildings in the city, including 800 Fifth Avenue, with a total of 1.5 million square feet. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Eliot Spitzer wins state approval to demolish 985 Fifth Avenue rent-stabilized building.
Two-year delay ended; NYC Landmarks approved demolition in 2023.
Project converts 25-story rental to luxury condo; rent-stabilized units removed from supply.
stories.summary: Eliot Spitzer obtained New York State approval to end rent-stabilized leases at 985 Fifth Avenue, clearing the path to demolish the 25-story rental building and replace it with luxury condominiums. The approval came after a two-year delay and a lawsuit against the state's Division of Homes and Community Renewal, following NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission approval in 2023. Spitzer Enterprises has advanced designs through SLCE Architects despite the regulatory hold-up.
stories.impact: Rent-stabilized unit removal in Manhattan's Upper East Side signals long-term pressure on affordable rental supply; however, this conversion from rental to condo benefits the condo market, not multifamily development. For apartment developers, loss of stabilized units in high-barrier-to-entry submarkets like UES may reduce both competitive pressure from legacy buildings and occupancy of naturally-occurring affordable stock, potentially raising rents in nearby multifamily assets.

stories.title: OCVibe Adds Five Dining Concepts to $5B SoCal District
stories.excerpt: The Samueli family has added five more dining concepts to the 50,000-square-foot market hall set to open next year as part of the $5 billion mixed-use development called OCVibe surrounding the Honda Center in Anaheim, Calif. Don Churros Gomez, MFK | Modern Filipino Kitchen, Mojo, Pull & Roll and Gelato Paradiso are the five new food options, adding Mexican, Filipino, Northern Chinese and Italian menus to the 21-kitchen market hall named Katella Commons. They join a growing roster at OCVibe, which earlier added concepts from chefs behind Amiga Amore, Burritos La Palma, Evil Cooks, Manaao Thai Comfort Food and Darkroom Restaurant and Wine Bar. Beloved Los Angeles chef Roy Choi is also bringing his Best Friend restaurant to the district. OCVibe did not disclose the values of the leases or the sizes of each space. OCVibe Senior Vice President Scott Frick recently told Commercial Observer that the Samueli family’s ownership structure has allowed the project to take a hands-on approach to restaurant leasing. Ownership is funding Katella Commons down to the kitchen equipment, allowing tenants to avoid substantial upfront costs of fitting out the new spaces. “Any tenant that comes in doesn’t have to come in with capital to fit out the kitchen — basically bring in your own knives and we’ll turn on the menu boards,” Frick said. That strategy is part of a broader effort to make OCVibe a year-round destination rather than a district that comes alive only when professional hockey team the Anaheim Ducks are playing. Frick said the project’s residential, office, hotel and entertainment components are intended to create a Monday-through-Sunday customer base for restaurants and other tenants. Katella Commons is expected to open in early 2027, following the debut of OCVibe’s concert hall, which can accommodate 5,000 people. bullets: OCVibe Samueli mixed-use adds 5 dining concepts to 50K SF market hall.
Opening next year; part of $5 billion development around Honda Center, Anaheim.
21-kitchen Katella Commons growing with chef talent including Roy Choi.
stories.summary: The Samueli family added five dining concepts—Don Churros Gomez, MFK | Modern Filipino Kitchen, Mojo, Pull & Roll, and Gelato Paradiso—to Katella Commons, a 50,000 square foot market hall opening next year as part of the $5 billion OCVibe mixed-use development surrounding the Honda Center in Anaheim, California. The 21-kitchen hall also features restaurants from high-profile chefs including Roy Choi. OCVibe did not disclose lease values or space sizes, but the ownership structure has enabled hands-on curation of the food tenant roster.
stories.impact: This is primarily a retail/hospitality story with limited direct relevance to multifamily development. However, the $5 billion OCVibe development signals strong mixed-use infrastructure investment in Anaheim, which may drive residential demand via employment and lifestyle amenities; multifamily developers should monitor whether the project attracts higher-income tenants to nearby residential in the Anaheim market and assess proximity of future multifamily sites to Katella Commons and Honda Center–adjacent retail.

stories.title: Two Merritt 7 Office Properties Set for Residential Conversion
stories.excerpt: CBRE completed the sale of 101 and 201 Merritt 7, two Class A office buildings totaling 511,318 square feet in Norwalk, CT on behalf of seller Merritt 7 Venture LLC. A joint venture of Saber-Hightower LLC, Granoff Real Estate & Wind River Holdings plans to convert the two buildings into M7 Lofts, a 286-unit luxury apartment community with more than 55,000 square feet of amenity space. Vice chairman Jeffrey Dunne, first VP Eric Apfel, investment sales director Travis Langer and senior financial analyst Eric Greenberg of CBRE represented the seller and procured the purchaser. Bank OZK provided a $75.5-million senior construction loan to support the conversion of the buildings. Built in 1980 and 1982, the two buildings sit within the broader Merritt 7 office park. Under Norwalk’s 2023 comprehensive rezoning, the site carries an as-of-right residential density of up to 564 units, but Saber-Hightower’s plan calls for 286 loft-style units. bullets: Saber-Hightower JV acquires two Merritt 7 office buildings totaling 511K SF, Norwalk.
Plan: convert to 286-unit luxury loft apartments; $75.5M Bank OZK construction loan.
Norwalk 2023 rezoning allows up to 564 units as-of-right; under-densified by developer.
stories.summary: A joint venture of Saber-Hightower LLC, Granoff Real Estate, and Wind River Holdings acquired 101 and 201 Merritt 7, two Class A office buildings totaling 511,318 square feet in Norwalk, Connecticut, for conversion into M7 Lofts, a 286-unit luxury apartment community with 55,000+ square feet of amenity space. CBRE brokered the sale; Bank OZK provided a $75.5 million senior construction loan. The buildings, constructed in 1980 and 1982, sit within the Merritt 7 office park and operate under Norwalk's 2023 comprehensive rezoning, which allows up to 564 units as-of-right.
stories.impact: Office-to-residential conversion in Norwalk signals continued weakness in suburban Connecticut office demand and strong appetite for multifamily conversion capital. The developer's choice to deliver 286 units instead of 564 allowed by zoning suggests yield constraints or market absorption limits; Norwalk multifamily developers should note zoning headroom but expect competitive conversion play and monitor financed conversion spreads (acquisition + construction cost vs. exit value) to assess market timing and cost inflation.

stories.title: KCI Technologies, Inc. Set to Occupy 53K-SF at Maryland Business Park
stories.excerpt: KCI Technologies, Inc. (KCI), a professional services firm with nearly 70 regional offices across 20 states and the District of Columbia, has signed a lease with St. John Properties, Inc. for 53,344 square feet at the North Park business community in Hunt Valley, Maryland. The firm plans to relocate its headquarters from Sparks to North Park, where it will occupy two and one-half floors at 6 North Park Drive. Approximately 300 KCI employees are expected to make the move in the second quarter of 2027. St. John Properties Leasing Representative Stephanie Caronna represented the landlord, and Joe Bradley and Mark Deering of MacKenzie Commercial Real Estate Services handled negotiations on behalf of the tenant. North Park features on-site amenities including a conference center with kitchenette, fully-equipped fitness center, walking trails, and a full-service cafe. The business community offers convenient access to abundant retail and dining options, including the adjacent Hunt Valley Towne Centre, a mixed-use project anchored by Wegmans Food Markets. The post KCI Technologies, Inc. Set to Occupy 53K-SF at Maryland Business Park appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: KCI Technologies relocates HQ from Sparks to Hunt Valley, Maryland; 53K SF lease.
300 employees moving to 6 North Park Drive in Q2 2027; St. John Properties landlord.
Professional services firm; offices in 20 states; HQ consolidation signal.
stories.summary: KCI Technologies, a professional services firm with nearly 70 regional offices across 20 states and D.C., leased 53,344 square feet at St. John Properties' North Park business community in Hunt Valley, Maryland, and plans to relocate its headquarters from Sparks. Approximately 300 KCI employees will move in Q2 2027, occupying two and one-half floors at 6 North Park Drive. North Park offers on-site amenities including a conference center, fitness center, and cafe, plus adjacent Hunt Valley Towne Centre retail.
stories.impact: HQ relocation of 300 employees from Sparks (west of Baltimore) to Hunt Valley (northeast) signals regional consolidation and job-cluster formation in the Hunt Valley/Towson submarket. This modest employment anchor may signal emerging office-park-to-mixed-use conversion activity and rising residential demand in nearby Hunt Valley submarkets; multifamily developers should assess proximity to North Park and the adjacent Towne Centre for capturing relocating employees and monitor whether further HQ consolidations accelerate Baltimore County multifamily absorption.

stories.title: New-Construction Quincy Apartments Sell for $13.5M
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap finalized the sale of The Willard, a 30-unit multifamily property located at 510 Willard St. in Quincy, MA. The asset sold for $13.5 million. “The Willard is a newly constructed boutique luxury apartment building that offers investors a high-quality, turnkey asset featuring modern finishes, spacious floor plans, quartz countertops, in-unit laundry, and separately metered utilities including water,” said Evan Griffith, senior managing director in Marcus & Millichap’s Boston office. Added Tony Pepdjonovic, senior managing director, “Located just off Interstate 93, this commuter-friendly Quincy location provides convenient access to local amenities as well as downtown Boston. We continue to see investors target high-quality locations with strong fundamentals. This property was 100% occupied at the close of escrow.” Pepdjonovic and Griffith exclusively marketed the property on behalf of the seller. The property was built in 2025, with a unit mix of 24 two-bedroom and six three-bedroom apartments. The property is situated in South Quincy, approximately nine miles south of Boston. The post New-Construction Quincy Apartments Sell for $13.5M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: The Willard, new-construction 30-unit apartment, Quincy, MA, sells for $13.5M.
Built 2025; 24 two-BR, 6 three-BR units; 100% occupied at close.

stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap finalized the sale of The Willard, a newly constructed 30-unit luxury apartment building at 510 Willard Street in Quincy, Massachusetts, for $13.5 million. The property features modern finishes, in-unit laundry, and separately metered utilities. The unit mix comprises 24 two-bedroom and 6 three-bedroom apartments; the building was 100% occupied at close of escrow. The South Quincy location, approximately 9 miles south of downtown Boston, offers convenient I-93 access and local amenities.
stories.impact: New-construction, fully-leased, 30-unit boutique asset in Quincy commands $450K per unit—a proxy for healthy fundamentals in the Boston South Shore suburban corridor. This signals sustained demand for commuter-friendly multifamily near I-93; multifamily developers should monitor Quincy's rental absorption, wage growth, and in-migration from Boston proper to inform future site acquisition and underwriting in Route 128–adjacent submarkets.

stories.title: Newly Built Mountain View Offices Secure $147M Financing
stories.excerpt: CBRE arranged $147.5 million in financing for 750 Moffett, a newly completed 221,788-square-foot Class A office property in Mountain View. The building is fully leased to an investment-grade technology company. A CBRE Debt & Structured Finance team led by Mike Walker, Brad Zampa and Andy Gross, arranged the financing on behalf of Genesis Commercial Capital and JR-AMC. The non-recourse financing combined senior debt and Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) financing to refinance existing debt prior to loan maturity. “The financing demonstrates continued capital availability for high-quality office assets with strong tenancy and long-term income characteristics, even as lenders maintain disciplined underwriting standards,” said Walker, an EVP with CBRE. Located near Moffett Park in Mountain View, 750 Moffett is a LEED Platinum-certified office building designed to meet the evolving needs of leading technology occupiers. The property is positioned within one of Silicon Valley’s leading innovation corridors, according to CBRE. The post Newly Built Mountain View Offices Secure $147M Financing appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CBRE arranges $147.5M financing for 750 Moffett, fully leased Class A office, Mountain View.
221,788 SF; newly completed; investment-grade tech tenant; LEED Platinum.

stories.summary: CBRE arranged $147.5 million in non-recourse financing for 750 Moffett, a newly completed 221,788 square foot Class A office building in Mountain View, California, fully leased to an investment-grade technology company. The financing combined senior debt and Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) financing to refinance existing debt prior to loan maturity. The LEED Platinum-certified building is positioned within Silicon Valley's innovation corridor near Moffett Park.
stories.impact: Continued capital availability for high-quality, fully-leased office with strong tenancy signals lender confidence in tech-anchored office fundamentals; however, this does NOT support multifamily development. Instead, robust office refinancing in Silicon Valley may attract capital away from multifamily and lock in office-to-residential conversion spreads; monitor whether sustained office valuations reduce conversion-play appetite in Mountain View and nearby Silicon Valley submarkets.

stories.title: The New School Sells Loeb Hall Residence to Hawkins Way Capital for $52M
stories.excerpt: In its third acquisition of student housing in Manhattan this summer, Hawkins Way Capital has purchased a residence hall near Union Square for $51.5 million from the New School, according to city records made public Tuesday. Hawkins, using the entity 135 E 12th Owner, bought Loeb Hall, a 268-bed residence hall at 131-135 East 12th Street, directly from The New School, records show. Joshua Bird, managing director and general counsel at Hawkins, signed the deal for the buyer, while Loretta Ferrari, chief financial officer at the New School, signed for the seller. “We’ve long been looking for the right opportunity in this neighborhood, and this property represents an ideal addition to our portfolio,” Ross Walker, managing partner at Hawkins, said in a statement to Commercial Observer. “Its location, existing student housing infrastructure and flexibility put us in an ideal position to deliver high-quality accommodations in one of the country’s strongest urban student housing markets.” It’s unclear why the New School stopped using Loeb Hall as an active dormitory for its students, but the property was removed from its undergraduate housing options this year. Loeb Hall is four blocks east of the New School’s main University Center and administrative offices on Fifth Avenue, although the sprawling urban campus has numerous sites near Union Square. The former Loeb Hall will undergo renovations and be repositioned under Hawkins’ Found Study student housing platform, according to a spokesperson for Hawkins. It’s unclear who brokered the recent sale. A spokesperson for the New School did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The deal is Hawkins’ third major student housing acquisition in Manhattan in recent months. bullets: Hawkins Way Capital acquires Loeb Hall, 268-bed student housing, Manhattan, for $51.5M.

stories.summary: Hawkins Way Capital purchased Loeb Hall, a 268-bed residence hall at 131-135 East 12th Street near Union Square, from The New School for $51.5 million, marking the firm's third student housing acquisition in Manhattan this summer. The acquisition reflects Hawkins' confidence in the neighborhood's student housing fundamentals and the property's location, existing infrastructure, and operational flexibility.
stories.impact: Institutional capital surge into Manhattan student housing signals tight supply and strong rents in a high-barrier-to-entry submarket. While this is a niche segment, the capital deployment and three-acquisition sprint suggest portfolio consolidation of student-oriented properties and may constrain multifamily developers' land and financing availability near NYU, CUNY, and New School campuses; conversely, higher student-housing prices may improve returns on adjacent multifamily conversions if young-professional rentership remains strong in the Lower East Side.

stories.title: Fifth Third, CB&T TruAmerica Lend $124M on Bay Area Apartments Build
stories.excerpt: SummerHill Apartment Communities (SHAC) has landed $123.5 million of construction financing to build a multifamily project in the San Francisco Bay Area, Commercial Observer has learned. Fifth Third Bank and California Bank & Trust (CB&T) provided a $96.5 million senior construction loan for the developer’s planned apartment community in San Carlos, Calif. TruAmerica Multifamily also closed a $27 million preferred equity investment to support the six-story San Mateo County development, which is slated to commence construction soon. The deal marked TruAmerica Multifamily’s first preferred equity financing since launching a structured finance platform last year. The new business vertical was formed following the addition of Ash Baraghoush, head of TruAmerica’s structured finance group, after he spent nearly a decade at Pacific Urban Investors. “This really goes hand in hand with the firm’s transformation into being a residential investment management company and being able to speak throughout the entire capital stack as opposed to just being owner operators,” Baraghoush told Commercial Observer. “We have spent a good year-plus cultivating new relationships.” Located at 11 El Camino Real 24 miles south of Downtown San Francisco, the project will feature 251 apartments with 38 of the units designated as affordable housing. Baraghoush said San Carlos has plenty of tailwinds as a multifamily market given its close ties to the San Francisco Bay Area’s technology and life science industries. He noted that the San Carlos submarket has a 97 percent multifamily occupancy rate and the region has experienced double-digit rent growth. “The Bay Area as a market has certainly outperformed and is perhaps one of the one of the better performing markets in the nation right now driven by return to office and driven by the AI boom,” Baraghoush said. “The need for affordable workforce housing continues to remain and that’s one of the attractive natures for this
bullets: SummerHill secures $123.5M construction financing for Bay Area apartments, San Carlos.
Fifth Third Bank, CB&T provide $96.5M senior loan; TruAmerica $27M preferred equity.
Six-story development; TruAmerica's first preferred-equity deal since launching structured finance.
stories.summary: SummerHill Apartment Communities (SHAC) landed $123.5 million in construction financing for a multifamily development in San Carlos, California, in the San Francisco Bay Area. Fifth Third Bank and California Bank & Trust (CB&T) provided a $96.5 million senior construction loan; TruAmerica Multifamily closed a $27 million preferred equity investment. The six-story development is slated to commence construction soon and marks TruAmerica Multifamily's first structured-finance deployment since launching its preferred-equity platform.
stories.impact: Strong construction-financing availability and preferred-equity capital entry (TruAmerica's new platform) signal continued lender confidence in Bay Area multifamily despite rate environment; however, the split 78/22 (senior/preferred) ratio suggests typical leverage discipline. Multifamily developers in San Carlos and nearby San Mateo County submarkets should note open capital channels and monitor whether TruAmerica's platform expansion attracts competitive preferred-equity pricing and accelerates starts in supply-constrained Silicon Valley markets.
